clue.text: Dick Bach's unusual bird

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of these letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer's name followed by a remark that he is a peculiar sort of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S stands for 'is', a link; the letters of DICK BACH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The dabchick is the little grebe, a small diving waterfowl.

clue.text: Fly with parent, having extended parts of journey?

parts.note: daddy is a father, a parent
extended means long
legs are stages of a journey

explanation.surface: A trip with Dad that has drawn-out stages.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a daddy-long-legs is a crane fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly is an insect with very long thin legs, called by this nickname.

clue.text: Musicians taking a long time dressing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Players are slow to get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a dressing put on a wound.

clue.text: Boundary hidden at first: I've found it!

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of discovery

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a border that had been concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch bounding a garden or park.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha forms a boundary without blocking the view, a fence in a trench.

clue.text: Sound of shopkeeper in basement

indicators.note: sound of means the answer is pronounced like the next word's synonym

parts.note: a shopkeeper is a seller

explanation.surface: A trader's noise is heard downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground storage room, a basement.

clue.text: Nimble artist federation's holding back

indicators.note: back tells us the concealed letters are read in the reverse direction
the words artist federation are holding the answer within them

explanation.surface: A nimble art body is said to be holding something back.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters TFED straddle 'artist' and 'federation'; reading them backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft and nimble are synonyms for quick and skilful movement.

clue.text: I hesitate to say some poetic lines are wearing

parts.note: er is a hesitant sound
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: A shy critic admits some verse is tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like tiring, an adjective; here it is a verb, wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something away gradually.

clue.text: Outrageously overrates true valuable find

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wildly overstates the worth of a genuine discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is buried gold or valuables discovered with no known owner.

clue.text: Spooner's suspended herb in filthy place

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial letters of the two pieces are exchanged

parts.note: suspended means hung
dill is a herb

explanation.surface: A herb has been hung up in a dirty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNG DILL with its first letters swapped becomes DUNG HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of manure is a byword for a squalid, dirty place.

clue.text: In French, I must grasp fine gag

indicators.note: must grasp means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the French word for I is je
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A French speaker insists on understanding a good gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is a comic remark or jest, a synonym.

clue.text: Bantu warriors: two grabbing member of parliament

indicators.note: grabbing means the first piece seizes the second within it

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Two tribal fighters seize a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a regiment of Zulu soldiers, Zulu being a Bantu people.

clue.text: Twelve months is long, endless

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: A complaint that a year drags on without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar year consists of twelve months.

clue.text: Being collected from class, men misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving letters are out of order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher stays composed while the men of a class act up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being collected means being composed and serene, which is calmness.

clue.text: Musical works being aspiration of Cockney artist's

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H sound at the start of a word

parts.note: an aspiration is a hope
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Musical pieces said to reflect a London painter's ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' also hints at the breathed H that Cockneys drop; a Cockney says 'ope for hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are staged dramatic works set to music.

clue.text: Touch on an objection?

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, like an
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should raise a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Two properties abut when they border or adjoin each other.

clue.text: Heard of one using tongue for strong drink?

indicators.note: heard tells us the answer sounds like the word described when spoken

parts.note: someone who licks is a licker

explanation.surface: A question about what someone who tastes with the tongue might drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is distilled alcohol, a spirit or other strong drink.

clue.text: Acceptable to tidy, as food left?

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially acceptable
to neaten is to tidy

explanation.surface: Whether it's fine to clear away leftovers on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U are labels for upper-class and not, popularised by Nancy Mitford.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been left on the plate has not been consumed.

clue.text: Cat made of iron cable

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a line is a cable or wire

explanation.surface: A sculpture of a cat fashioned from metal wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline as a noun means a member of the cat family.

clue.text: Ogreish thug reels, regularly making signs

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A brutish thug staggers about while making signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures are movements of the hands or body used as signals.

clue.text: Our brief to be welcomed by half a dozen native Americans

indicators.note: to be welcomed by means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: half a dozen is six

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: Six people are greeting us.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are a group of Native American peoples of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Animal doctor holding son's garment

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: a vet treats animals
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A vet keeps hold of a boy's item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A vest in Britain is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is an item of clothing worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Guide visiting Australia

parts.note: visiting a place is being at it
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A tour leader on a trip Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: The A to Z is a well-known British street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: An A to Z is a street map book, or more broadly a comprehensive guide.

clue.text: Which are in the conceited, for example, outsize?

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what big, oversized things vain people carry inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited people are said to have inflated self-images, swollen senses of self.

clue.text: Knocked off witty number

indicators.note: knocked about, these letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever number has been dashed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty-two is an integer, the count of cards in a deck.

clue.text: Alluring, singular, old partner seen with Yankee

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an ex is a former partner
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A single person's former lover is spotted with an American, and looks attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy means sexually attractive, enticing.

clue.text: Feeling of regret after taking in variable Cornish resort

indicators.note: taking in means the first piece absorbs the second

parts.note: penance is sorrow shown for wrongdoing
Z is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Remorse after accepting something changeable.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Penzance is a seaside town in Cornwall, a holiday destination.
